en: Regarding the image of Hayagrīva:
furthermore, take a clean cloth that has not been cut or trimmed. Invite a most skilled painter; do not pay him his fee.
Have him bathe in fragrant water, dress in new, clean garments, and bestow upon him the eight precepts for the day. Day.
It is thus. In a pure place, construct a water mandala four cubits in length and breadth.

Having performed the methods for the water mandala as described in other sections, and having completed the mantra-practitioner’s protection of the body and the binding of the boundary (*sīmābandha*), [proceed].
Having burned various kinds of incense and scattered various kinds of flowers as offerings within that maṇḍala,
one should draw a bodhisattva inside this maṇḍala.
The body is one span (vitasti) taller than the Buddha; its height and length are exactly equal to one human cubit (hasta). It has four faces in total.
The central Bodhisattva face must be made extremely upright and handsome, with an expression of compassion, a complexion of reddish-white, and hair that is purely blue-black.
The face on the left side is intensely wrathful, black in color,
with fangs protruding upward and hair standing slightly erect like the color of flames.
The face on the right side displays a great laughing expression.
Red and white, upright and handsome like the face of a bodhisattva;
his hair is purely blue, and upon each of his three faces he wears a celestial crown and earrings.
Upon his celestial crown is a manifested Buddha seated in the full lotus posture.
On the crown of the central face, there is a green horse head with its mouth closed.
Below the neck of the Bodhisattva, he wears a jeweled necklace.
The nape of the neck and the back are adorned with circular halos composed of several layers of color.
His left arm is bent, and his hand rests before his breast grasping a red lotus flower;
this lotus is level with the Bodhisattva’s head and positioned directly over his left shoulder.
Upon the flower pedestal, there is a manifested Buddha wearing a crimson kāṣāya, seated in the full lotus posture,
with light radiating from his neck and back.
The right hand has its palm facing upward with the five fingers extended;
the arm and elbow are bent at equal angles.
The palm holds a cintāmaṇi (translated into Chinese as "wish-fulfilling jewel"), which is spherical and white in color.
A red-colored flame encircles the jewel.
From his right hand, which is positioned directly over the jewel, various kinds of treasures rain down.
Upon his left shoulder...
Regarding the *cīvaraka* (worn on the shoulder): it is made of tiger skin, as translated into Chinese;
it should be worn like a *saṃkakṣikā*, covering the area under the right armpit and secured with a tie, and further, tiger skin should be used to cover the upper part of the hips.
The outer armlets, celestial garments, skirts,
and so forth are all to be depicted according to the method for painting bodhisattvas found elsewhere;
specifically, they should be portrayed with bodies upright and straight, standing upon red lotuses.
A precious parasol hangs suspended above the head of the Bodhisattva.
In the sky above it, various celestial musical instruments are depicted.
On both sides in the air, gods of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens perform dances as offerings.
When painting this image, use fragrant resin juice;
animal glue must not be used.
Furthermore, grind the seeds of *sumukha*—translated into Chinese as *yuntai* (mustard)—into a powder.
Make it extremely fine using the residual whey from curdled milk;
mix it according to the method for mixing flour.
Use the *Haya-grīva* heart-mantra.
After reciting the mantra twenty-one times,
the patient shall remain with an empty stomach;
all venomous insects within the abdomen will then be completely vomited up.
Furthermore, regarding the method for painting images: take a new,
unused ceramic jar and dye it blue.
On the earthenware jar, one should paint an image of Avalokiteśvara, Āryāvalokiteśvara.
The height of the image should be one *vitasti* of the Tathāgata, or one *hasta* of a human; it should be depicted with four joyful faces.
The left side is painted black;
the pupils of the eyes are green, and canine fangs protrude from the mouth.
The right side is painted red.
This is called the "Mantra-Facing" (Zhòumiàn).
The central front face should be made into a bodhisattva face,
rendered as extremely upright and handsome.
Paint it white. Above the crown of the image, it should be suspended in mid-air.
Paint it with a blue face.
From his mouth he spat out precious pearls.
Upon each of his four heads he wore a jeweled crown,
and upon each crown sat a manifested Buddha.
The Bodhisattva holds a lotus flower in his left hand,
bending the elbow upward to cradle it before his shoulder;
his right arm hangs down with all five fingers extended.
The hand displays the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*). Both wrists are adorned with jeweled bracelets,
and the image wears a jeweled necklace around its neck.
The adornment of the body is as described elsewhere regarding the methods for adorning the body of Avalokiteśvara.
This image should be depicted standing upon a precious lotus flower.
Having fashioned this image, [one should proceed].
Beginning on the tenth day of the waxing moon, he consumed a gruel of barley and milk;
thereafter, on the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days,
he fasted for three days and three nights.
Take the *sāgabhiccha* incense and the *kandhanajuli* flower;
recite the mantra over each of these two substances once and cast them before one’s face, repeating this up to eight thousand times.
From his face and mouth, he emits a great radiance that encircles the body of the mantra-practitioner,
then returns and enters the mouth of the image.
From his mouth, a wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi) emerged;
he immediately took it, and having obtained the jewel,
his lifespan was extended to fourteen thousand years.
They shall become wheel-turning sage-kings of the seven treasures,
and after their lives end, they will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
sitting at the feet of Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, there is another method: one should go on almsround and eat only barley milk gruel while reciting [the mantra] seventy thousand times.
When ten thousand recitations have been completed, the Vināyaka will immediately be bound.
At the second ten thousand recitations, the mantra method is accomplished.
At the third ten thousand recitations, one attains the accomplishment of the *āśanāmānasthira* medicinal formula.
One shall not eat for three days and three nights.
When performing the ritual, the practitioner holds the medicine in their hand;
while reciting the mantra over the medicine,
if three kinds of signs appear within it:
One then knows that the medicine has been perfected.
The three signs are heat, smoke, and flame.
Thus one attains the accomplishment of the *āntaradhāna* [power of invisibility].
Ascending into the air and departing, one attains the accomplishment of a mantra-holding ṛṣi;
with mastery, one gains entry into the palace of the asuras.
At the fourth stage of ten thousand recitations, one can travel four finger-widths above the ground with complete freedom.
At the fiftieth thousand recitations, one will attain the power to ascend and travel through the air at will.
At the sixtieth thousand recitations, one will immediately attain a lifespan of a thousand years;
the mantra-practitioner becomes an accomplished mantra-rishi.
Whatever a person does will be spontaneously accomplished;
all those who are summoned will come.
Upon reaching seventy thousand recitations, the mantra master’s hair will transform into spiral locks, and he will achieve accomplishment.
Whatever they may require arrives as soon as it is thought of.
By drawing near to and serving Avalokiteśvara,
they immediately come to know the deaths and rebirths of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time.
One will immediately achieve success.
Furthermore, if one wishes to strike [the enemy] with a sound like "xi" (pronounced as in "xiāo") or "yè" (pronounced as in "yé"),
one should fast for three days and three nights before an image of Hayagrīva and smear the altar with incense.
With various kinds of incense and flowers,
and with pure offerings of food, milk-rice, fruits, and so forth,
one should pound *sāgaracandana* incense.
Mix white honey to form eight thousand pills.
After reciting the mantra over one pill once,
cast it into the fire to burn.
When the incense was thus exhausted,
that assembly of yakṣas immediately saw [the deity] first transform into Hayagrīva (Horse-Head).
After a short while had passed...
When the mantra-practitioner, with his gaze directed upward toward that assembly, transforms [the state] into a *kharvara*,
the entire host of *siddhas* is completely dispersed and extinguished.
Furthermore, according to another method, first give barley to a cow to eat.
Then, take the barley from its dung, wash it until dry, and grind it thoroughly before boiling it into milk gruel (*kṣīrayaṣṭi*).
Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, consume this milk gruel.
On the thirteenth day, he immediately ceased eating.
Before the image of Hayagrīva,
he smeared the ground with fragrant ointment and scattered various kinds of flowers.
Having finished making offerings of various incenses and diverse foods and drinks,
take *kāpiśā* incense and grind it into a fine powder.
Mix the water with the powder to form pills;
when the count reaches eight thousand,
take kādara wood to serve as fuel and kindle a fire.
Take one incense pellet, recite the mantra once,
and cast it into the fire;
continue in this manner until eight thousand pellets have been offered.
The charcoal will be completely transformed into suvarṇa gold, weighing one hundred thousand *liang*.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to consume the mantras of others.
Having taken a small amount of blood from one's own body,
mix it with white mustard seeds to form eight thousand pills.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
Having fasted for one day,
he takes *khadira* wood and kindles a fire in a brazier;
he then takes the previously mentioned white mustard seed pills.
Recite one mantra for each pill and cast them into the fire until all the mustard-seed-sized pills are exhausted.
"All mantras shall be entirely consumed"— the word "consumed" (k'i) is a foreign term.
This is identical to the terminology used when the Great Tang was destroyed.
"The others" refers to non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*). Furthermore, as for the Dharma, they merely recite mantras while traveling through wildernesses and various sandy deserts.
The food and drink required will emerge spontaneously. Furthermore,
according to another method, during a solar or lunar eclipse,
take one *liang* of pure cow’s ghee and place it in a new earthen bowl.
He then held up this bowl to gaze at the sun and moon,
and recited mantras over the ghee within it until the ghee grew warm,
or smoke and fire issued forth.
At that time, one should drink this ghee; having consumed this ghee, wherever one wishes to go, one will arrive as soon as the thought arises.
If one constantly recites this mantra, [the same result shall follow].
One shall attain fearlessness amidst all terrors and be completely liberated from all obstacles and difficulties.

Furthermore, regarding this dharma: if one suffers from a *rūḍha* ulcer—an ulcer that invariably leads to death—or is bitten by various venomous snakes, such that the person dies upon seeing the snake; or if one suffers from a *kambīṭa* ulcer.
For these various sores, one should recite the mantra over yellow earth and mud one thousand times;
by applying it to the sores, they will be immediately healed.
All fears and anxieties shall be immediately dispelled upon recollecting this.
Furthermore, if a person should suddenly encounter any peril involving water,
by recollecting this, they shall not be submerged or drowned.
Such dharmas as these cannot be explained in detail;
they are accomplished according to one's wish.
If one constructs a great maṇḍala:
One must not engage in sexual desire.
For the *haya-karṇa* healing illness mudrā: form the inner fist with both hands, extend the two middle fingers so their tips touch each other, and bend the two thumbs together.
With each hand, bend the two index fingers to grasp the base of the two thumbs;

the tips of the nails should all touch their backs. Recite: Oṃ hulu lu-julu dhana svāhā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā hāye gṛhapati-bhikṣu-mudrā. For the *gṛhapati-bhikṣu* mudrā, turn the left hand upward and extend all five fingers vertically.
Turn the right hand downward and touch the tips of the middle and ring fingers together;
recite "Oṃ naye" twice seven times. The two mudrās mentioned above may follow the sequence of the *kṣepaṇī* (releasing) sword mudrā.
If one performs this rite, one should first bind and restrain the vināyakas.
One should do so before an image of Hayagrīva,
taking a piece of *khadira* wood eight finger-widths long and cutting it.
When flames emerge from the fire,
take *guggulu* incense and fashion eight hundred pills.
Recite the mantra once for each pill and cast one into the fire.
Until the fragrance is exhausted,
the Vināyakas shall bind themselves, pronouncing this mantra:

Homage to Tadyathā (1) cūru cūru (2) vicūru cūru (3) gadaye svāhā (4) mahāparakara (5) sarvavicinavijayaṅga (6) bhaṭṭapramukta (7) pūtaye phaṭ (8). If a person discharges impurity at night, [they should recite this].
Take white thread and recite the mantra over it eight hundred times.
Afterwards, fashion a mantra-cord;
for each recitation, make one knot, until there are twenty-one knots.
Then he tied it around his waist so that nothing would be lost again.
The mantra is as follows:

Homage to Tadyathā: (1) bṛti bṛti, (2) subṛti, (3) indrarbṛti, (4) māme śukāraṃ, (5) brahmavatsadu, (6) svāhā. Furthermore, there is a method for reciting this dhāraṇī over a *kāṣāya* robe seven times.
Having already tied it into a single knot, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the body-protection mantra.

The verse for taking refuge is as follows: *Tadyathā:* 1. *Hare* 2. *Hare* 3. *Muhare* 4. *Guhare* 5. *Sarvatusthāṃ* 6. *Campaye* 7. *Nayabhaṅgandhe* 8. *Navañcami* 9. *Svāhā* [End of the above. Following this, recite the sequence for the attainment of efficacy. This concludes the *Haya-grīva-vidhi*. (Note: The transliteration provided follows the standard IAST conventions for Sanskrit, with the exception of the specific phonetic notation used in the source text for certain aspirated and retroflex sounds.)
